name: Yingzhao / 英招
evidence: 神英招司之，其狀馬身而人面，虎文而鳥翼。
originalAdaptation: Age 24, handsome human male proportions, horse ears/tail as equine humanization, facial design, garments and palette are original adaptation. Main text attests horse body/human face/tiger markings/bird wings; it does not attest horns or this clothing.
identity: SHJ-037 Yingzhao, a strikingly handsome lean young adult man age 24. Long angular human face, firm narrow jaw, long straight nose rendered as one tiny wedge, thick sharply angled brows, narrow flat amber eyes and a daring tooth-showing crooked grin. His hair is warm chestnut in large swept-back mane-like locks and a short low tied section, with two real tall chestnut HORSE EARS arising from his scalp; no horns and no human ear duplication. Genuine dark tiger stripes occur in the skin on his cheeks, neck and exposed upper arms, not fabric graphics. Two real large BIRD WINGS grow from his shoulder blades: flat cream main feathers, dark umber outer tips, simplified broad grouped feathers. A real long dark horse tail grows from the base of his spine and curves visibly beside his hip; hair tuft at tail end, not a costume sash. Slim deep forest-green sleeveless wrap tunic with a high asymmetric ivory inner collar, muted terracotta waist sash, dark fitted trousers. Modest natural physique, not a bulky warrior. View A left: frontal upper-thigh portrait, one brow lifted and mouth slanted open; wings relaxed outward. View B right: three-quarter upper-thigh portrait turned toward viewer, shoulder rotated enough to see organic wing roots and horse-tail attachment, same alert grin. Keep faces large and legible, complete wings and horse tail within the sheet. This is original humanization of horse-bodied mythology: no centaur lower body required, but horse ears/tail, organic tiger markings and true feather wings must be unmistakable.
